children: Electric two-wheelers accounted for nearly one in every 10 two-wheelers sold in India during April-August FY27, even as the Centre approved the deployment of ₹776.29 crore to strengthen testing infrastructure for electric vehicles and other emerging automotive technologies, senior government officials said on Friday.

The figures were disclosed at the PM E-Drive Dialogue with the Industry at ICAT in Manesar, presided over by Heavy Industries Minister H D Kumaraswamy on Friday as part of the automotive testing agency’s 20th anniversary programme.

Kumaraswamy called for closer collaboration among testing agencies, vehicle manufacturers, component suppliers, and researchers as India develops new automotive technologies and strengthens its manufacturing capabilities.

“We have sanctioned ₹776 crore for upgrading the testing agencies under PM E-Drive,” Heavy Industries Additional Secretary Hanif Qureshi said. The investment covers ICAT in Manesar, ARAI in Pune, GARC in Chennai, and NATRAX in Indore and is aimed at preparing them for electric vehicles, batteries, clean technologies, and advanced automotive components.

With India already the world’s largest producer of two-and three-wheelers, Qureshi said manufacturers and testing agencies need to work together on technologies that can also support exports. “We have to move towards Make in India for the World,” he said.

PM E-Drive’s outlay has been raised to ₹11,900 crore, while incentives for electric two-wheelers have been extended until March 2028. The program's target for the segment has increased from 24.8 lakh to 45.8 lakh vehicles.

Electric two-wheeler penetration reached 9.9 per cent during April–August FY27, up from 6.6 per cent in FY26, Suneet Shukla, chief general manager at IFCI, said. Electric L5 three-wheelers accounted for 46.1 per cent of their segment during the period, compared with 31.7 per cent in FY26.
Qureshi also said ICAT generated a ₹142-crore profit last year, which he cited as evidence of the progress made by India’s automotive testing infrastructure.

“When NATRIP was conceived in 2005, the initial sanction was ₹1,700 crore for setting up three testing centres. It was subsequently enhanced to around ₹3,700 crore,” he said. The objective was to create world-class testing facilities that could support the industry and eventually become self-sustainable.
Kumaraswamy also inaugurated an indigenously developed 100 kN load car, an agricultural-machinery testing facility, and a lift-capacity facility for tractors.
“A practical constraint in tractor performance testing was identified and addressed through an in-house engineering solution,” Kumaraswamy said.

The load car applies controlled resistance while a tractor pulls it, enabling engineers to measure pulling power, wheel slip and fuel consumption under repeatable conditions. The new facilities are expected to improve testing availability and make certification schedules more predictable.

title: Electric two-wheeler penetration nears 10%; Centre allocates ₹776 crore to upgrade EV testing infrastructure
